text.p: American Educational Products Inc said it renegotiated both its short- and long-term credit facilities with Colorado National Bank, substantially reducing its principal payments.

The multi-media and educational materials developer and producer also said its board of directors approved a private securities offering of up to 500,000 units at a price of $1.00 per unit. A unit consists of one common share and one warrant to purchase another share at $1 per share, it said.
The offering is aimed at reducing debt and creating working capital, it said, adding it has already received funds for 2000,000 units, which it used to reduce debt.

The company said its $1.5 million revolving credit line used for working capital was extended to April 30, 1997 and more debt of about $1.4 million was restructured into a $400,000 mortgage and a $1 million term note with a maturity date extended to January 31, 1998.
After the restructuring, the company also said about $300,000 previously classified as a current liability was reclassified as long-term debt.
Clifford Thygesen, president, said: "Our banking agreements solve many of the cash flow problems that have resulted from the company's operating losses during 1994 and 1995."
